page.layout: One column of text. Top: continuation paragraph of the previous page. Below it: the division heading "CONCIO LX.", the scripture reference "1. Petri 3.", and the opening paragraph with a large woodcut initial S. No margin notes. No text below the column.

main_text.p: dies accidere videmus. Punit illos Deus, conjugii vindex, morbis, egestate, orbitate, & fere illorum posteritas extinguitur, qui spuriis suis urbes totas replere videbantur. Misericors & omnipotens Deus convertat nos ab omni immunditia ad veram sanctimoniam, sine qua nemo videbit Dominum (Hebraeorum duodecimo) ut liberemur ab ira ventura, per Iesum Christum Dominum, & castissimae virginis filium, Amen.
main_text.head: CONCIO LX.
1. Petri 3.
main_text.p: Similiter uxores subdita sitis vestris viris, ut etiam qui non obtemperant sermoni, per uxorum conversationem absque sermone lucrifiant: dum considerant cum reverentia conjunctam castam conversationem vestram, quarum ornatus sit non externus, qui situs est in plicatura capillorum, et additione auri, aut in palliorum amictu: verum occultus, qui est in corde homo, si is careat omni corruptela, ita ut spiritus pla[?]

page.notes: The scan is slightly blurred. "subdita sitis" is read as printed, with the long s and ligatures transcribed as plain s; the word after "subdita" is uncertain. "si is" at the end of the line is uncertain, and "careat" is read from a partly damaged word. The last word "pla" is cut off at the line end and continues on the next page, so it is marked [?]. The heading "CONCIO LX." and the reference "1. Petri 3." are set apart and are treated as level 1 and level 3 respectively. The left margin has small marks and a faint mark at the page edge, which are not printed text and are not transcribed.
